$comment: Primary-source oracle — taxable-interest / yield-character / basis cases: bank/CD interest is annual ordinary income, brokerage yield splits by explicit tax character, cash-like principal withdrawals are untaxed return of already-taxed dollars, and the assumed-cost-basis fraction drives the LTCG proxy. Expected values derived independently from the cited sources; never from production code.

irs-tc403.name: IRS Topic no. 403 — Interest received
irs-tc403.identifier: Interest on bank accounts, money market accounts, and certificates of deposit is taxable ordinary income in the year it becomes available; principal itself is not re-taxed

usc-1411.name: 26 U.S.C. §1411 — Net investment income tax
usc-1411.identifier: Interest and dividends are net investment income; NIIT applies only above the MAGI threshold

irs-ir-2025-103.name: IRS IR-2025-103 — tax year 2026 annual inflation adjustments
irs-ir-2025-103.identifier: 2026 Single brackets + $16,100 standard deduction; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 LTCG 0% band to $49,450 (Single)

yield-assumption.name: Repo calibration assumption — assumed taxable-account yield (2% total, 50% qualified-dividend, 0% municipal)
yield-assumption.publication: population-level planning assumption, asOfDate 2026-06-10 (no single authoritative source; disclosed, not statutory)
yield-assumption.identifier: yield = 2% of the brokerage-like start balance; half qualified dividends, half ordinary interest; municipal share 0 unless explicitly calibrated

cases.description: 2026 Single filer (age 55): $3,500 bank/CD interest taxed as ordinary income, $200,000 brokerage balance throws 2% assumed yield split QDI/ordinary, $20,000 brokerage sale with a 60% cost-basis fraction, and a $10,000 cash-like principal withdrawal contributing $0 to income or MAGI.
derivation: Assumed yield = 2% * 200,000 = 4,000 -> 2,000 QDI (LTCG-rate stack) + 2,000 ordinary interest + 0 municipal.
LTCG/QDI = 20,000 * (1 - 0.60) + 2,000 = 10,000. Ordinary income = 40,000 other + 2,000 yield interest + 3,500 cash interest = 45,500.
Taxable income = 45,500 + 10,000 - 16,100 = 39,400; taxable ordinary = 29,400 -> tax = 1,240 + 12%*17,000 = 3,280.00; LTCG stacks entirely inside the 0% band (39,400 < 49,450) -> $0.
MAGI = 45,500 + 10,000 = 55,500 — the $10,000 cash-like principal withdrawal adds NOTHING (already-taxed principal; its growth was taxed annually as interest per Topic 403).

cases.description: Direction check: removing the $3,500 annual cash interest lowers ordinary income dollar-for-dollar — annual interest taxation is a real drag, not a wash.
cases.tolerance: within $1; direction asserted separately (tax WITH interest > tax WITHOUT)
derivation: Same case with cashInterestDollars 0: ordinary = 42,000; taxable income = 35,900; taxable ordinary = 25,900 -> tax = 1,240 + 12%*13,500 = 2,860.00.
MAGI = 42,000 + 10,000 = 52,000. Delta vs the with-interest case = 12% * 3,500 = 420.00 of extra tax.
